_review: Meadow chapter, part 1: the fire night at Hearn (user plan 2026-10-22). Merged into frost.json's data by game/chapter.js mergeChapters; one quest graph. Ids are meadow-*; flags are meadow:*. Dialogue follows docs/village/dialogue-style.md: plain, who/what/where, objectives as imperatives. Coordinates of places come from data/world/village.json (tests pin them).
title: The Burning Night

npcs.name: Wenna
npcs.about: A young woman of Hearn with a lantern. Ran north for help. Leads the Wraith to the burning village.

npcs.name: Marit
npcs.about: Ebb's mother. Stands in the square and calls at his house.

npcs.name: Ebb
npcs.about: Marit's six-year-old son. Hides in the burning house.

npcs.name: Hild
npcs.about: Elder of Hearn. Gives the Wraith leave to climb the stair.

npcs.name: Corin
npcs.about: Looking for his brother Alder, who was taken.

npcs.name: Garrow
npcs.about: The smith of Hearn. Keeps the cold forge and raises Shaper weapons for marks and what the hills give.

npcs.name: Doran
npcs.about: Watches the foot of the stair and lets no one climb.

npcs.name: Alder
npcs.about: Corin's brother, a shepherd. Taken up the hill on the night of the fire; held in the manor's forecourt by the Bellwether's bell until it is released.

npcs.name: Senna
npcs.about: Maud's apprentice, fourteen. Went out to the old loom-house on the Western Edge for Maud's shuttles and is caught in the Wind Gap, behind its last stone (systems/windGap.js).

npcs.name: Wenna
npcs.about: Wenna, gone south after the Bellwether's release: at the Wellhouse camp in the dunes (systems/travel.js).

npcs.name: Doran
npcs.about: Doran, if he came back down from the manor: gone south with Wenna (systems/travel.js).

npcs.name: Tamsin
npcs.about: Hild's granddaughter. Taken up the hill with Alder; kept him talking so he would not sleep.

caller: The roof is going! We need water!
Someone, please! This house is full of smoke!
Over here! Get the water over here!
bucket: It is not enough. It is never enough.
huddle: Do not look at it. Look at me.
marit: Ebb! Ebb, can you hear me?
My son is in that house!
corin: Alder! Alder, can you hear me?
guideWait: Please, wait for me! No, I mean — come on!
Are you coming? We have to hurry!
guideArrive: This is Hearn. Look at the roofs!

meadow.ebb.gateman.speaker: meadow-ebb
lines: Before the fire, the gate-man came to our house. Doran.
He had a big jar. It smelled like the lamps.
He told me to go to bed and stay in bed. So I did.

meadow.doran.confess-rag.speaker: meadow-doran
lines: That rag is from my gate. Then you know.
I set the fires. Not the Shaped. I did.
I wanted Hearn awake and afraid, and nobody on the hill road when you came.
My daughter Bryn is up at the manor. She climbed the stair to see the bell, forty years ago. She was sixteen.
The bell stopped, and she never came down. Whatever is up there, you will kill it. Then it is over, for her too.
I did not know Ebb was in that house. I swear it.

meadow.doran.confess-ebb.speaker: meadow-doran
lines: Ebb told you about the jar. Then you know.
I set the fires. Not the Shaped. I did.
I wanted Hearn awake and afraid, and nobody on the hill road when you came.
My daughter Bryn is up at the manor. She climbed the stair to see the bell, forty years ago. She was sixteen.
The bell stopped, and she never came down. Whatever is up there, you will kill it. Then it is over, for her too.
I did not know Ebb was in that house. I swear it.

meadow.doran.after.speaker: meadow-doran
lines: Tell Hild, if you have to. I will not run from Hearn.
But do not go up that hill. Please.

meadow.doran.daughter.speaker: meadow-doran
lines: You have been up at the manor. Did you see anyone up there?

options.text: Tell him about the girl at the window, with the lamp.

meadow.doran.wait.speaker: meadow-doran
lines: A girl with a lamp. That is Bryn. That is my Bryn.
Wait one night before you go back up. Let me climb first and say goodbye to her.
One night. Then do what you came to do.

meadow.doran.back.speaker: meadow-doran
lines: I held her hand. It was cold, and she did not know me.
I told her everything anyway. Then I came down, like I said I would.
I cannot stay under that hill. I am going south with Wenna.

meadow.doran.exile.speaker: meadow-doran
lines: You. Did Hild send you after me?
No. You only came north. Everyone does, in the end.
The fire here is good. Isolde lit it. I sit by it, and I think about Bryn.

meadow.hild.rag.speaker: meadow-hild
lines: You have something in your hand. It smells of lamp oil.
Where did you find that?

options.text: Give Hild the rag, and tell her it was behind the stair gate.

meadow.hild.doran.speaker: meadow-hild
lines: Behind the stair gate. Doran keeps that gate, and Doran keeps the oil.
Ebb could have burned in that house. Marit could have lost him.
Doran leaves Hearn tonight. He goes north, and he does not come back.

meadow.wenna.plea.speaker: meadow-wenna
lines: Please — the village is burning! I am Wenna, from Hearn.
Shaped came down from the hill at dusk. They set the houses on fire.
You are the first person I have found out here. Please, help us. Follow me!

meadow.wenna.hurry.speaker: meadow-wenna
lines: Hearn is south of here, down the road. Stay close to me!

meadow.wenna.here.speaker: meadow-wenna
lines: This is Hearn. Please, put out the fires. Elder Hild is at the hall.

meadow.wenna.after.speaker: meadow-wenna
lines: Hearn is still standing because of you. Thank you.

meadow.marit.plea.speaker: meadow-marit
lines: I am Marit. My son Ebb is still inside! That is our house, there.
He is six years old. He hides when he is afraid. Please, bring him out!

meadow.marit.thanks.speaker: meadow-marit
lines: Ebb is safe. I will not forget this.

meadow.ebb.cower.speaker: meadow-ebb
lines: I am Ebb. Please do not go! The roof is making noises.
Are you here to take me out? Okay. I will stay right behind you.
Lead me to my mum. She is in the square.

meadow.ebb.behind.speaker: meadow-ebb
lines: I am right behind you. Do not walk too fast.

meadow.ebb.home.speaker: meadow-ebb
lines: Mum says I was brave. I was not. I was very scared.

meadow.hild.fires.speaker: meadow-hild
lines: I am Hild, elder of Hearn. The fires come first. Put out as many as you can.
And Marit's son is still in his house. Please help her.

meadow.hild.ebb.speaker: meadow-hild
lines: The fires are out, but Ebb is still in Marit's house. Please, bring him out first.

meadow.hild.thanks.speaker: meadow-hild
lines: The fires are out. Ebb is safe. Thank you.
I am Hild, elder of Hearn. I will tell you plainly what happened tonight.
The Shaped came down from the hill at dusk. They carried fire, and they set our roofs alight.
They took two people with them: Alder, a shepherd, and Tamsin, my granddaughter.
We searched the hill road. We found only footprints, going up.
No one has climbed the stair in years. We were afraid of it. But you have proved yourself.
The stair is yours. Go up the hill, and bring them home if you can.

meadow.hild.after.speaker: meadow-hild
lines: The stair is open to you. Alder and Tamsin are somewhere up there. Please find them.

meadow.corin.search.speaker: meadow-corin
lines: Have you seen my brother? I am Corin. My brother Alder was with the sheep on the hill road.
He did not come back. I have looked at every door in Hearn. He is not here.
They took him. I know they took him.

meadow.corin.after.speaker: meadow-corin
lines: Hild says you may climb the stair. Please look for Alder. He is tall, with a brown coat and a shepherd's crook.
While you look: I saved what I could from the fire. Salves, and Peg's bread. Marks, if you have any. The old silver still counts.

meadow.garrow.raid.speaker: meadow-garrow
lines: The forge can wait. Go to the fires. I will bring a bucket when the line gets to me.

meadow.garrow.forge.speaker: meadow-garrow
lines: I am Garrow. I keep the forge of Hearn. It went cold at the first frost and I never lit it again.
You carry Shaper work. I can feel it from here. Bring me marks and what the hills give, rime and hedge-heart and amber, and I will make it better.
Some tiers teach a weapon a new move. Some only add weight. I will tell you which before you pay.

meadow.wenna.south.speaker: meadow-wenna-south
lines: You found me. I could not stay in Hearn after the wind came back.
Everyone kept thanking me, and all I did was run north and find you.
Sarai says the well here was full once. I want to see that.

meadow.wenna.south-doran.speaker: meadow-wenna-south
lines: You found me. I could not stay in Hearn after the wind came back.
Doran came with me. He does not say much. He says you let him go up and see her first.
Sarai says the well here was full once. We both want to see that.

meadow.wenna.south-again.speaker: meadow-wenna-south
lines: The sand gets into everything. I do not mind it.

meadow.doran.south.speaker: meadow-doran
lines: The hill is a long way behind me now.
I keep the camp's gate here. Nobody asks me why.

meadow.ketil.beacon.speaker: meadow-ketil
lines: There is another light I keep: the old Lake Beacon, on the shoulder west of the lake.
Its three iron shutters stuck the night the bell stopped. Rust, or something worse. No light gets out.
I am too old to climb it now. Climb it and strike the shutters open, and I will light it again.

meadow.ketil.beacon-done.speaker: meadow-ketil
lines: I saw it from the square. All three shutters open.
My grandfather said the bell's neck has shutters like those. Valves, he called them. Three of them, up the neck and round it.
You can only strike them open from the neck itself, he said. I will light the beacon tonight.

meadow.maud.senna.speaker: meadow-maud
lines: I am Maud, the weaver. My apprentice Senna went out to the old loom-house on the Western Edge, for my good shuttles.
The wind has gone wrong up there since the bell stopped. It holds its breath, and then it throws itself up the gap all at once.
She has not come back. The Wind Gap is west of the lake, where the Edge drops to the sea. Please, find her.

meadow.maud.senna-home.speaker: meadow-maud
lines: Senna is home. She says you kept the stones between you and the wind.
That is how the bell's wind used to come, before it stopped. In, and then all at once.
If anything ever breathes at you like that, keep stone between you and it.

meadow.senna.found.speaker: meadow-senna
lines: I am Senna. Did Maud send you? I cannot go back through that.
When the grass leans toward the sea, it is coming. Then it hits like a wall.
Go first, stone to stone. I will follow you when it has gone past.

meadow.senna.follow.speaker: meadow-senna
lines: Stone to stone. I am right behind you.

meadow.senna.home.speaker: meadow-senna
lines: I am going home. I am never fetching shuttles again.

meadow.garrow.flue.speaker: meadow-garrow
lines: The forge would draw again if the old flue drew. The manor's kilns sent their smoke under the hill, out through three vents in the forest north of the manor.
When the kilns burned, that draught pulled through my forge too. It has been dead since the bell stopped.
Turf has grown over the vents. Go and pull it off, and I will light the forge.

meadow.garrow.lit.speaker: meadow-garrow
lines: I felt it before you came in. The forge is pulling air again.
Doran's girl worked those kilns, before. Bryn. She used to bring me the iron they could not use.
The chimneys on the manor hall are sealed the same way, with turf. They are too high for hands. You would need a wind.

meadow.doran.block.speaker: meadow-doran
lines: Stop. I am Doran. I watch the foot of the stair.
No one goes up there. Not since the Shaped began coming down it.
Ask Elder Hild. Only she can say who climbs.

meadow.doran.open.speaker: meadow-doran
lines: Elder Hild says you may climb. I am sorry I stopped you.
Go on, and be careful. The stair is long, and what took our people is at the top.

meadow.alder.found.speaker: meadow-alder
lines: You are not one of them. Good.
I was with the sheep. Then the bell started, and I could not move. I heard it the whole time.
Tamsin was next to me. She kept talking, so I would not go to sleep.
Is it over? Then I am going home. Tell Corin I am coming.

meadow.alder.wait.speaker: meadow-alder
lines: I can walk. Give me a moment, and I will be right behind you.

meadow.alder.home.speaker: meadow-alder
lines: Corin has not let go of my arm since I got back.
The sheep will have gone everywhere. I do not care.

meadow.tamsin.found.speaker: meadow-tamsin
lines: Do not help me up yet. My legs are asleep.
Grandmother sent you? Of course she did.
Go on. I can walk down on my own.

meadow.tamsin.wait.speaker: meadow-tamsin
lines: I said I can walk. Go on.

meadow.tamsin.home.speaker: meadow-tamsin
lines: Grandmother cried when she saw me. Do not tell anyone.

meadow.hild.released.speaker: meadow-hild
lines: The bell has stopped. I can hear the wind on the hill again.
But Tamsin is not home, and nor is Alder. If they are anywhere, they are up at the manor. Please, go and look.

meadow.hild.home.speaker: meadow-hild
lines: Tamsin is home. So is Alder. You gave them back to us.
The wind is moving on the hill again. Hearn owes you more than we can pay.

meadow.corin.released.speaker: meadow-corin
lines: The bell has stopped. Did you see Alder up there? Please, go back and look.

meadow.corin.alder.speaker: meadow-corin
lines: He came down the stair on his own two legs.
I do not know what you are. Thank you.

quests.title: The Lake Beacon
quests.summary: The Lake Beacon's three iron shutters stuck shut the night the bell stopped. Ketil is too old to climb it.

steps.journal: Climb the Lake Beacon, west of the lake, and strike its three shutters open. Hold the traverse to grip; climb up, down and round it.
The shutters are open. Tell Ketil in Hearn.

quests.title: The Wind Gap
quests.summary: Maud's apprentice Senna went out to the Western Edge and has not come back. The wind comes up the gap there in fits since the bell stopped.

steps.journal: Find Senna in the Wind Gap, on the Western Edge west of the lake. When the grass leans toward the sea, get behind a stone.
Lead Senna back up the gap, stone to stone. She follows when a gust has passed.

goal.label: The top of the Wind Gap

steps.journal: Senna is safe. Tell Maud in Hearn.

quests.title: The Cold Forge
quests.summary: Garrow's forge in Hearn drew its air from the manor's old kiln flue. Turf has sealed the flue's three vents in the forest.

steps.journal: Pull the turf off the three vents of the old flue, in the forest north of the manor.
The flue is breathing. Tell Garrow in Hearn.

quests.title: The Burning Night
quests.summary: A woman begs you to follow her. Her village, Hearn, is on fire.

steps.journal: Talk to Wenna, the woman with the lantern, on the north road.
Follow Wenna to the village of Hearn. Stay close to her.
Put out the fires in Hearn. Use Ribbon or Sweep on the burning roofs.
Bring Ebb out of the burning house. His mother, Marit, is in the square.
Talk to Elder Hild at the hall.
Climb the stair to the manor at the top of the hill.
Go to the manor's forecourt. Something inside it is waking up.
Free the Bellwether. Blow the turf off its three chimneys with Gust (look up at one and tap Q), then climb its neck and strike the three valves.
Go back down to Hearn. Tell Elder Hild what happened, and find Alder and Tamsin if they are not home yet.

optional.journal: Talk to Marit in the square. She is calling for her son.

quests.title: Alder
quests.summary: Corin cannot find his brother. The Shaped took him up the hill.

steps.journal: Talk to Corin in Hearn. He is looking for his brother Alder.
Climb the stair behind Hearn. The Shaped took Alder up the hill.
Find Alder on the hill. Whatever took him is in the manor.

meadow-lore-beacon.title: The Lake Beacon
meadow-lore-beacon.text: An old column of stacked stone on the shoulder west of the lake, leaning out over the water, with an iron lamp-cage at its head. Three iron shutters on its flanks let the light out across the meadow. They stuck shut the night the bell stopped.

meadow-lore-gap.title: The Wind Gap
meadow-lore-gap.text: Since the bell stopped, the sea wind comes up the Western Edge in fits. The air in the gap is drawn toward the sea, and then it comes back all at once, like a wall. The old stones in the gap are the only shelter.

meadow-lore-flue.title: The Kiln Flue
meadow-lore-flue.text: The manor's kilns ran their smoke under the hill and out of three vents in the forest. Their draught pulled through Garrow's forge in Hearn. When the bell stopped, the kilns went cold, and turf grew over the vents.

meadow-lore-raid.title: The Raid on Hearn
meadow-lore-raid.text: At dusk the Shaped came down the hill road with fire and set the roofs of Hearn alight. They took two people, Alder the shepherd and Tamsin, the elder's granddaughter, and went back up the hill. As told by Hild.

meadow-clue-gate.name: The stair gate
meadow-clue-gate.title: The stair gate
meadow-clue-gate.text: A rag is stuffed behind the gate post, soaked in lamp oil. Dark drips run from the gate down the path toward the houses. You take the rag.

meadow-clue-window.name: The hall window
meadow-clue-window.title: The hall window
meadow-clue-window.text: A girl stands at the window, in a kiln-worker's apron, a lamp in her hand. She does not move. The flame does not move either.

lines: Tamsin is back. I did not think I would see her again.
I keep looking up at the hill. Tamsin is up there.
Thank you again. I do not have anything to give you.
I will find Hild. Please, the fires first.
Doran went up the hill before the bell stopped. He did not come down.
Nobody keeps the stair gate now. Nobody needs to.
Tamsin, sit down. You have walked enough for one week.
Tamsin has her mother's temper. She will be fighting them still.
Fires first. Then we will count who is missing.
Alder, eat something. You are grey.
Alder knows every path on that hill. If he can run, he is running.
Alder! Alder, answer me!
It goes up the hill, it kills what is up there. You do not know what is up there.
Leave the hill alone. Hearn has burned enough tonight.
Mind the steps. There are over eight hundred of them.
He keeps his hands in his sleeves. The cloth round them is wet.
Nobody climbs. Those are Hild's orders.
Doran. He sat at my table every winter. He held Ebb when he was born.
I am not letting go of him tonight.
Ebb! Ebb, please!
We will rebuild. We always do.
The well is half empty already.
The thatch will take all summer to mend.
Pass the bucket! Pass it along!
My house is only half burnt. I am lucky.
That is the baker's roof! Someone help!
They came so fast. I did not even see their faces.
Look at the sparks! They are jumping from roof to roof!
I cannot stop smelling smoke.
Stay low. Stay with me.
I have lived here seventy years. I never saw the Shaped come down before tonight.
It is the hill. The hill has woken up.
Are the monsters gone?
I want to go home. But home is on fire.
Ebb says he was not scared. He is lying.
Is Ebb out yet? Is he out?
Count us again, Hild. Please. Just once more.
Two of us are gone. Two. I counted.
Come to my shop when you are back. There will be bread.
My shop! My whole shop!
